## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates your ability to design and implement distributed tracing across a multi-datacenter Docker Swarm environment while meeting strict performance requirements and handling TLS/Nginx integration complexities.

## Key Concepts

- OpenTelemetry instrumentation and configuration
- W3C trace context propagation across service boundaries
- OTLP (OpenTelemetry Protocol) exporters and data flow
- Jaeger backend integration for trace storage and visualization
- Docker secrets and configs for secure configuration management
- Multi-datacenter deployment considerations and latency optimization
- Sidecar patterns for collector deployment
- Performance monitoring and overhead control strategies

## Code Example

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml skeleton for distributed tracing
version: '3.8'
services:
  api:
    image: my-api:latest
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
    environment:
      - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=otel-collector:4317
      - OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=my-api
      - OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.name=my-api
    depends_on:
      - otel-collector
  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:latest
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    volumes:
      - ./otel-collector-config.yml:/etc/otelcol-contrib/config.yaml
    command: ["--config=/etc/otelcol-contrib/config.yaml"]

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question validates the ability to design and implement per-tenant service mesh policies in a multi-data center environment, with emphasis on dynamic policy reloads, zero-downtime updates, and strong tenant isolation.

## Key Concepts

- Consul Connect per-tenant service identities and mTLS
- Envoy sidecar injection and Traefik as an edge proxy
- Dynamic policy storage in Consul KV with hot-reload via consul-template
- Multi-data center architecture considerations and zero-downtime updates

## Code Example

```yaml
version: '3.9'
services:
  traefik:
    image: traefik:v3.0
    command:
      - --providers.consulcatalog
      - --providers.consulcatalog.endpoint.address=consul:8500
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./traefik-dynamic.yml:/dynamic.yml:ro
    environment:
      - CONSUL_HTTP_ADDR=consul:8500

  consul:
    image: consul:1.17
    command: agent -server -ui -bootstrap-expect=1 -client=0.0.0.0
    ports:
      - "8500:8500"

  consul-template:
    image: hashicorp/consul-template:latest
    command: -consul-addr=consul:8500 -template "/tmp/intentions.hcl:/etc/consul-intentions/intentions.hcl:consul reload"
    volumes:
      - ./intentions.ctmpl:/tmp/intentions.hcl

  backend-tenant-a:
    image: your-backend:latest
    labels:
      - "consul.hashicorp.com/service=api-tenant-a"
      - "consul.hashicorp.com/enable-ingress-gateway=true"

  backend-tenant-b:
    image: your-backend:latest
    labels:
      - "consul.hashicorp.com/service=api-tenant-b"
```

## Bootstrap Commands

```bash
# Initialize Consul agent
consul agent -config-dir=/etc/consul.d &

# Register services with Consul
consul services register -name=api-tenant-a -id=api-tenant-a
consul services register -name=api-tenant-b -id=api-tenant-b

# Create intentions for tenant isolation
consul intention create -deny "tenant-failing" "api-tenant-a"
consul intention create -allow "tenant-permitted" "api-tenant-a"

# Enable Envoy sidecar injection
consul connect envoy -sidecar-for api-tenant-a -register &

# Reload Traefik on policy changes
consul-template -template=intentions.ctmpl -exec="traefik --reload"
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests edge proxy TLS termination, simple per-tenant rate limiting, and Docker Compose orchestration across DCs. It stays beginner-friendly while touching operational concerns.

## Key Concepts
- TLS termination at the edge
- Nginx limit_req for per-tenant rates
- Tenant discovery via HTTP header
- Docker Compose skeleton for cross-DC deployments

## Code Example
```nginx
# nginx.conf
http {
  map $http_x_tenant $limit {
    default 1r/s;
    'tenantA' 5r/s;
    'tenantB' 2r/s;
  }
  limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=per_tenant:10m rate=$limit;
  server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    location /api { limit_req zone=per_tenant burst=10; proxy_pass http://api:8080; }
  }
}
```

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml skeleton
version: 3.8
services:
  nginx:
    image: nginx:latest
    ports: ["443:443"]
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
      - ./certs:/etc/ssl/certs:ro
  api:
    image: your-api
  loader:
    image: alpine:latest
    command: sh -c 'cp /config/tenant_limits.json /nginx/tenant_limits.json'
    volumes:
      - ./config/tenant_limits.json:/config/tenant_limits.json:ro
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example
```lua
-- Redis Lua script: token bucket (simplified)
local key = KEYS[1]
local refill = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local limit = tonumber(ARGV[2])
local tokens = tonumber(redis.call('GET', key) or '0')
local max = 1000
local new_tokens = math.min(tokens + refill, max)
if new_tokens < 1 then
  return {1, new_tokens}
end
new_tokens = new_tokens - 1
redis.call('SET', key, new_tokens)
return {0, new_tokens}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement zero-trust security, multi-tenant isolation, and safe deployment patterns in Docker Swarm with policy-as-code enforcement.

## Key Concepts
- Swarm secrets/configs for secure data management
- Sidecar pattern for policy enforcement and logging
- Canary deployments with automatic rollback
- TLS termination at edge proxy
- OPA for real-time authorization decisions

## Code Example
```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports: ['443:443']
    secrets:
      - source: tls-cert
        target: /etc/nginx/ssl/tls.crt
      - source: tls-key
        target: /etc/nginx/ssl/tls.key
    configs:
      - source: nginx-conf
        target: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
      restart_policy:
        condition: on-failure
        delay: 5s
        max_attempts: 3
    networks:
      - frontend

  api:
    image: my-api:latest
    environment:
      - TENANT_CONFIGS=/configs/acls.json
    configs:
      - source: tenant-acls
        target: /configs/acls.json
    deploy:
      replicas: 5
      update_config:
        parallelism: 1
        delay: 15s
        failure_action: rollback
        monitor: 30s
        max_failure_ratio: 0.2
      rollback_config:
        parallelism: 1
        delay: 10s
      healthcheck:
        test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8080/health"]
        interval: 10s
        timeout: 5s
        retries: 3
        start_period: 30s
    networks:
      - frontend
      - backend
    volumes:
      - audit-logs:/var/log/audit

  opa:
    image: openpolicyagent/opa:latest
    command: ["run", "--server", "/policies/policy.rego"]
    configs:
      - source: opa-policy
        target: /policies/policy.rego
    environment:
      - OPA_LOG_LEVEL=info
    networks:
      - backend
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8181/v1/data"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3

  log-collector:
    image: fluent/fluent-bit:latest
    command: ["/fluent-bit/bin/fluent-bit", "--config", "/fluent-bit/etc/fluent-bit.conf"]
    volumes:
      - audit-logs:/var/log/audit
      - ./fluent-bit.conf:/fluent-bit/etc/fluent-bit.conf:ro
    networks:
      - backend
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
      restart_policy:
        condition: on-failure

secrets:
  tls-cert:
    external: true
  tls-key:
    external: true

configs:
  nginx-conf:
    external: true
  opa-policy:
    external: true
  tenant-acls:
    external: true

volumes:
  audit-logs:
    driver: local

networks:
  frontend:
    driver: overlay
  backend:
    driver: overlay
    internal: true
```

## fluent-bit.conf
```ini
[SERVICE]
    Flush         5
    Log_Level     info
    Daemon        off

[INPUT]
    Name          tail
    Path          /var/log/audit/*.log
    Tag           audit.*
    Refresh_Interval 10

[OUTPUT]
    Name          file
    Match         audit.*
    Path          /var/log/processed
    File          audit.log
```

## Implementation Details

**OPA Integration**: OPA sidecar loads policies from Docker config and exposes authorization endpoint at `http://localhost:8181/v1/data`. API checks authorization before processing requests.

**Canary Strategy**: 20% rollout (1 out of 5 replicas) every 15 seconds with 30-second health monitoring. Automatic rollback on >20% failures.

**Security**: TLS termination at Nginx edge, secrets management for certificates, internal backend network isolation, per-tenant ACL enforcement.

**Logging**: Audit logs written to shared volume, processed by fluent-bit sidecar for aggregation and forwarding.

local rate = tonumber(ARGV[2])

app = Flask(__name__)
flag = False

def load_flag():
    global flag
    try:
        with open('/config/flag.json') as f:

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to design cross-DC coordination for tenant-scoped migrations, focusing on correctness, failover semantics, and idempotency under failure conditions.

## Key Concepts
- **Per-tenant migrations and versioning**: Each tenant has an isolated migration state tracked via an `applied_version` table, enabling independent progression and rollback.
- **Redis-based distributed locking**: Serializes migration runs to prevent concurrent execution against the same tenant DB, using `SET NX EX` for atomic lock acquisition with TTL-based deadlock prevention.
- **Cross-DC failover and home-DC preference**: The pipeline attempts the home DC first, detects connectivity failures, and transparently fails over to the secondary DC while maintaining lock continuity.
- **Idempotent SQL migrations**: Each migration file is versioned and checked before execution; repeated runs against an already-migrated tenant are no-ops.
- **Docker Compose wiring across two DCs**: Each DC runs an independent `docker-compose.yml` with shared Redis (Cluster or Sentinel) and per-tenant database containers.

## Bootstrap Commands
```bash
# Initialize tenant migration table
psql $TENANT_DB_URL -c "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations (version INT PRIMARY KEY, applied_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW());"

# Run migrations for a tenant
docker-compose run --rm migrator --tenant-id <id>

# Manual lock acquisition for debugging
redis-cli SET tenant:<id>:migrate 1 NX EX 300
```

## Minimal docker-compose.yml Skeleton
```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  migrator:
    image: migrator:latest
    environment:
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis-cluster:6379
      - HOME_DC=${HOME_DC:-dc1}
    depends_on:
      - redis-cluster
    volumes:
      - ./migrations:/app/migrations:ro

  redis-cluster:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    command: redis-server --cluster-enabled yes --cluster-config-file nodes.conf
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
```

## Code Example
```javascript
// Redis-backed rate limiter pseudo implementation
async function checkRateLimit(tenantId) {
  const key = `ratelimit:${tenantId}`;
  const limit = await redis.get(`${key}:limit`) || 100;
  const window = 60; // seconds

  const current = await redis.incr(key);
  if (current === 1) {
    await redis.expire(key, window);
  }

  if (current > limit) {
    throw new Error('429 Too Many Requests');
  }
  return current;
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Evaluates image provenance, canary sequencing, and Swarm upgrade semantics in a multi-datacenter setup.

## Key Concepts
- Image signing with cosign and DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST
- Swarm update_config for controlled upgrades
- Traffic splitting via an in-cluster reverse proxy (Traefik)
- Canary pattern and safe rollback in production

## Code Example
```javascript
// illustrative docker-compose-like snippet (Traefik routing hints)
services:
  api-v1:
    image: registry.example.com/api:v1
    deploy:
      replicas: 4
      labels:
        - "traefik.enable=true"
        - "traefik.http.routers.api-v1.rule=Host(`api.example.com` )"
  api-v2-canary:
    image: registry.example.com/api:v2-canary
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
      labels:
        - "traefik.enable=true"
        - "traefik.http.routers.api-v2-canary.rule=Host(`canary.api.example.com` )"
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would key rotation and automatic signing verification be automated?
- How would you measure canary health and decide promotion/rollback automatically?
